text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
* If the government ends the practice of employing civil servants on "precarious" contracts, 15,000 positions will be added to the official workforce from April 30.

* About 130 workers of the Sao Jacinto shipyard in Aveiro in central Portugal run the risk of having their work contracts suspended by September unless funds are made available for the construction of fishing boats.
* "There is no justification to reduce the number of MPs," said Francisco Assis, the next parliamentary leader of the ruling Socialist Party, discussing constitutional reforms.
* The district of Gois near Coimbra in central Portugal hit by forest fires. Usually Portugal does not suffer from forest fires until much later in the year.
* The government under-estimated debts owed to the social security department at December 31, 1995 by 96 billion escudos.
* Mining company Somincor has revised upwards its 1997 results forecast to a profit of 800 million escudos from a loss of at least two billion escudos.
* Prime Minister Antonio Guterres wants to step up cooperation between government ministers and the parliamentary party.
